prompt: In the linker script pattern `.data : { ... } > RAM AT> FLASH`, what do the section's VMA and LMA represent, and why does `.bss` need no LMA at all?
choices: VMA is the runtime address the CPU reads/writes through (RAM); LMA is where the section's initial byte image is stored in flash for startup code to copy from. .bss has no LMA because it holds no initializer image -- it's just zeroed in place.
VMA and LMA are always identical; `AT> FLASH` only changes where `.text` is linked.
LMA is the RAM address used at runtime; VMA is the flash address used only during linking.
VMA is where the CPU executes code from; it only applies to `.text`, and `.data`/`.bss` never have a VMA.

prompt: GPIOC_CRH packs pins 8-15 into 32 bits, 4 bits per pin, so pin 13's MODE/CNF field sits at bits 23:20. Which code correctly configures PC13 as a push-pull output at 2 MHz (MODE13=10, CNF13=00), starting from an unknown reset state?
choices: GPIOC_CRH |= (0x2 << 20);
GPIOC_CRH &= ~(0xF << 20); GPIOC_CRH |= (0x2 << 20);
GPIOC_CRH = 0x2;
GPIOC_CRH |= (0xF << 20);

prompt: GPIOC_BSRR sets pin x via bit x (BSx, bits 0-15) and resets pin x via bit x+16 (BRx, bits 16-31), with 0 having no effect in either half. Which single write atomically drives PC13 LOW?
choices: GPIOC_BSRR = (1 << 13);
GPIOC_BSRR = (1 << 16);
GPIOC_BSRR = (1 << 29);
GPIOC_BSRR = 0xFFFF;

prompt: At reset, what does the Cortex-M3 core do with the first two words of the vector table?
choices: It loads the program counter from word 0 and the stack pointer from word 1.
It loads the stack pointer from word 0 and the program counter from word 1.
Both words are ignored until the first interrupt fires.
Word 0 holds the NMI handler and word 1 holds the reset handler; the stack pointer defaults to zero.

prompt: Why must startup code explicitly zero `.bss` rather than relying on RAM already being zero at power-on?
choices: RAM contents at power-on are not guaranteed to be zero or known, so skipping this step leaves uninitialized globals holding garbage.
.bss is stored in flash as a block of zero bytes that must be copied in, just like .data.
The linker already zeroes .bss at link time, so this step is purely defensive and never actually matters.
Cortex-M3 hardware zeroes SRAM automatically on every reset, so this step only matters on other architectures.

choices: The write is ignored -- GPIOC's bus clock is gated off, so the register doesn't latch the new value and reads back its reset state.
The CPU immediately raises a HardFault exception.

prompt: What is the correct order of operations inside Reset_Handler before branching to main()?
choices: Zero .bss, then copy .data from flash to RAM, then set the stack pointer.
Call main() first, then initialize .data and .bss from within main().
